1.1.name: Our resize rule matches Qwen's processor

1.2.name: Image rebuilt from the model's input numbers matches the resized image
1.2.detail: max difference 6.0e-08 on a 0–1 scale (pass < 1e-4); the 2 frames per patch are identical

1.3.name: Number of image tokens = rows × columns
1.3.detail: 345 image tokens in the prompt; grid 23 × 15 = 345

1.4.name: Qwen's own positions put token k at row k ÷ W, column k mod W

1.7.name: Encoder output k is what the language model receives in image slot k
1.7.detail: max difference 0.0e+00 (pass < 1e-3); each of the 345 slots is closest to its own encoder output

1.6.name: Token count stays under the configured budget

1.5.name: Changing one square changes that square's token the most
1.5.detail: 21 / 24 random squares. The changed square's token responded 0.37× to 2.85× as much as the next-largest (median 1.45×); weakest: row 13, column 12 (0.37×). The runner-up was an immediate neighbour in 19 of 24.

image._why: Qwen's own pixel budget (passed as size=). 401408 px = 512 x 28 x 28, so at most ~512 visual tokens, the scale of the pilot images. Note: the documented max_pixels= argument is silently ignored in transformers 5.11; only size= works (STAGES.md, stage 1).

generation.prompt_suffix: Explain your reasoning step by step, describing what you see in detail.
generation._why_suffix: Forces long answers: a short answer gives one eviction event and no timeline.

quant._why: KIVI-style: keys rounded per channel within blocks of 32 tokens. 16 = no rounding.

eviction._why: Cache budget = keep_frac x prompt length. The most recent tokens are never evicted (standard practice).

evidence._why: Evidence = visual tokens attended a lot in the last window_frac of the answer but little in the first. top_frac of visual tokens are kept. Answers shorter than min_steps are flagged, not measured.

stats._why: Significance threshold for the paired Wilcoxon tests. The results page words its verdicts from this.

stage1._why: Squares changed per image in the causal test (check 1.5). offline_pilot = which pilot image the offline stages page shows (index into pilot.items; 5 = the skier).
